## Gerrit 1398 pushed — RED->GREEN evidence and gate results

**Change 1398** (`9f26: report a dropped parent, don't lose it`), 4 files:

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py` | +31/-2 — `_resolve_local_parent` gains two keyword-only optional params and records `(jira_key, "parent")` on the existing `dropped_field_sink` when a BOUND non-epic parent is suppressed |
| `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_emit_suppression_is_loud_9f26.py` | new, 7 cells — the held-out RED oracle |
| `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` | the two re-homed live cells |
| `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` | +32 — the re-measured verdict with run id 30951453979 |

### The signature had to stay a 2-tuple

Two existing tests destructure `_resolve_local_parent`'s return and one asserts `== (False, None)`
exactly (`test_dc_live_oracles_discriminate_5200.py`, `test_dc_epic_link_parent_39c1.py`). A
3-tuple would have broken both, so the signal is an additive optional parameter. That is the
caller-dependency sweep result: those callers depend on the SUPPRESSION behaviour, which is
preserved — the parent is still omitted — so they are incidental to the change.

### RED -> GREEN, held out and mutation-checked

The oracle was moved OUT of the working tree before the implementer was launched; it only ever
saw the contract card (postcondition + 7 invariants), never the assertions or the path.

* **RED** (fix absent): 2 failed / 5 passed — failing on `dropped=[]`, the target assertion, not
  an import or fixture error. The 5 passing are invariant guards that must NOT change.
* **GREEN** (fix applied, oracle restored): 7 passed.
* **Mutation M1** — re-seed the exact root cause (bare silent `return (False, None)`): back to
  **2 failed**.
* **Mutation M2** — record UNCONDITIONALLY, collapsing the bound/unbound distinction: **1 failed**,
  the negative control.

M2 is worth recording as a process note: **it did NOT kill the first version of the oracle.** My
negative control used an *epic* unbound parent, which never enters the guarded branch at all, so a
fix that appended unconditionally would have passed. I reverted the fix, added a NON-epic unbound
case, re-proved RED in that final form, then re-applied — the strict order, because a test edited
alongside a fix proves nothing. The oracle was genuinely weaker than I claimed until that round.

### Gate exit codes (real, not piped through tail)

`make lint` **0** · `make typecheck` **0** (mypy, 432 files) ·
`pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` **0** —
10200 passed, 38 skipped (baseline on this worktree was 10185 passed; +7 are the new cells)

### Fix-safety audit

Restoration, not creation (completing 39c1 AC4 on a surface it was never wired to, legitimacy
`incomplete-implementation` with cited authority) · no new dependency · **no test weakened**:
assertion counts in the two re-homed cells went UP, 5->8 and 2->10, and no `skip`/`xfail` was
added anywhere.

### Parity sweep -> [rebar:8390-32f7-e4b8-48a1] (linked `discovered_from`)

The rule — "an outbound parent that cannot reach the tracker must leave a durable record" — has
four surfaces. Slot 1 (UPDATE emit) is closed here; slot 3 (UPDATE apply) already held via 39c1.
**Slots 2 and 4 are still MISSING**: the CREATE emit (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:145-156`)
signals only via `logger.debug`, and the ACLI create-then-attach fallback
(`acli_cli_ops.py:136-143`) swallows a 400 with a WARNING and no `record_parent_divergence`.
Filed rather than fixed because both reach into Cloud/ACLI adapters, outside this ticket's declared
`file_impact`. That ticket also carries the 8b25 guard's vendor-scoping doc/code divergence.

**Not closing this ticket** — the three cells only run in the live harness, so the acceptance
criteria need a harness run to verify.
